appraisal_events.evidence: "il parlait des propositions qu'on lui avait faites avec la même indignation que les journaux d'un vol à main armée"; "le monsieur battu était excusable"; "Saint-Loup eût donné sa raclée sans beaucoup réfléchir"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator frames Saint-Loup's violent overreaction to a proposition and his indignant, newspaper-style outrage as disproportionate, while noting the beaten man was 'excusable'; the initial aestheticized description of the punches as a beautiful spectacle also undercuts rather than endorses Saint-Loup's conduct.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's ironic framing of Saint-Loup's thoughtless violence and disproportionate indignation mildly deflates him, even as his physical beauty is affirmed.

ambiguities: The narrator's comparison of Saint-Loup's beating and indignation to newspaper outrage over armed robbery, combined with sympathy for the 'excusable' victim, is only mildly diminishing and could be read as neutral character description rather than pointed irony toward Saint-Loup himself.

Norpois is mentioned as implicitly more respectable than other women's lovers ('amants moins respectables que celui-ci'), but this comparison is used instrumentally to argue about Mme de Villeparisis's decline rather than to independently evaluate Norpois, so it was not scored as a distinct event.
